run: C5: does adding sentence-level data from google/smol help?
hypothesis: The corpus is 63% single Creole words while every benchmark is sentences, so adding 2,468 human-translated pairs with a median of 14 words should help out of domain.

corpus.note: 4 of the 2,472 dropped as exact duplicates. Zero overlap with either benchmark on either side under the loose leak key.

conclusion: The hypothesis was wrong. Adding SMOL costs 0.0048 nDCG@10 out of domain, which puts it below R4's worst seed and 2.2 seed standard deviations from its mean, against a measured run-to-run drift of 0.0024. In domain the difference is +0.0006, inside noise. Read alongside C2, where removing the dictionary also hurt, both directions of changing the corpus composition make the model worse, which suggests the corpus sits near a local optimum for this recipe.
caveats: One seed. R4 has three. The direction is clear and outside R4's observed range, but a single run cannot separate a real effect from an unlucky draw as precisely as three would.

SMOL grew the mining pool by 7%, so the hard negatives changed as well as the training data. Whether the loss comes from the added rows or from the mining shifting under them would need the volume-matched control C2 used.
SMOL is a different collection with a different register, so this measures adding that corpus rather than adding sentence-level data in general.
